messages.author: d1a299345e24af11
messages.subject: Fixed a coefficient
parts:
How to fix a non-zero coefficient in the structural model?
Why does the following does not fix the coefficient of b2 to 1?

library(lavaan)
d <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(1:3000), ncol=4, dimnames=list(NULL, c("y", "x1", "x2", "x3"))))

model1.syntax <- 'y ~ b1 * x1 + b2 * x2 + b3 * x3 + 0;
                  b2 == 1'
summary(sem(model1.syntax, data=d))

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Fixed a coefficient
parts:
There have been some recent changes in how lavaan handles constraints. It is possible that earlier versions of lavaan (<0.5-18) are handling constraints in a way that might cause an error (see this document for more information: http://lavaan.ugent.be/notes/lavaan_eq_constraints.pdf)

Regardless, there's an easier way to fix a parameter to a numeric value, just specify a number as the label, so your code would be:

model1.syntax <- 'y ~ 1 * x1 + b2 * x2 + b3 * x3 + 0'

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Fixed a coefficient
parts: Nope, converging after 1 iterations is likely due to the simplicity of the model (it is a linear regression model). Your code looks (mostly) correct. I think the + 0 at the end of the first line might be causing some problems (and it isn't affecting the model). You've specified the inequality constraint correctly, but you'll notice that the Slack for the inequality constrain is not close to 0 (Slack = 0 is a binding constraint, non 0 Slack means a constraint is either non-binding or impossible given the data).

messages.subject: Re: Fixed a coefficient
parts: Nope, converging after 1 iterations is likely due to the simplicity of the model (it is a linear regression model).

Indeed, as Alex pointed out, this is just a multiple regression model, in which case lavaan defaults to using the lm() function to return OLS results.  You can override this by using the option "fixed.x = FALSE", in which case you will see that your b2 coefficient is returned as 1 (because the data won't let it go any higher than that) with slack close to 0.  But the SE couldn't be computed for b2 when I ran it.

Terry

parts:
Does "model2.syntax" have no intercept? How come it gives the same estimate for b1, b2 and b3 as "model1.syntax", which has an intercept?
model1.syntax <- 'y ~ b1 * x1 + b2 * x2 + b3 * x3 + 1'
model2.syntax <- 'y ~ b1 * x1 + b2 * x2 + b3 * x3 '

You can fix the intercept to zero the same way you fix slopes to zero.  Either of these would work:

y ~ b1 * x1 + b2 * x2 + b3 * x3 + 0*1

or

y ~ b1 * x1 + b2 * x2 + b3 * x3 + a*1
a == 0

Terry
